description: The log specification — the single source of truth for what this repository logs, at what level, on which channel, and with which fields. A call site names an event id; the level, the channel, the message and the required fields come from here, so changing what is logged is a change to this file rather than a sweep through the code. Every channel here is the modelling tool's own. The generated application logs through Loco's `tracing` subscriber and does not read this file: it is a Rust crate, and a JSON catalogue it would have to parse at startup to say the same things `tracing` already says is a translation layer, not a shared contract.

transport.rationale: The application writes structured JSON to stdout and nothing else — no files, no rotation, no network. Whatever runs the process (Docker, Kubernetes, systemd, a log shipper) is what collects and ships it. A process that manages its own log files has to be configured twice, fills a disk nobody is watching, and blocks the event loop doing it.

redact.rationale: Redaction is declared once, here, rather than remembered at each call site. A credential reaches stdout exactly once before it is in a log aggregator forever, so the default is to censor by key name anywhere in the object rather than to trust every caller to strip it.

channels.name: db
channels.description: Database connection lifecycle and schema migrations. Individual successful queries are not events; a failure is.

channels.name: pipeline
channels.description: The code-generation pipeline: check the model, compile its directives, emit the application.

channels.name: auth
channels.description: Authentication outcomes for the modelling tool: sign-in, registration, refusal, rate limiting.

channels.name: ai
channels.description: Calls to the local model. A prompt and a completion are business data and are never logged.

channels.name: app
channels.description: Process lifecycle: an unhandled error reaching the top of the process, and shutdown on a signal.

channels.name: entity
channels.description: Business reads and writes in a generated application: promotion, the audit trail, and a value the row decoder could not read.

channels.name: rules
channels.description: Business-rule evaluation and the actions a matched rule performed.

channels.name: workflow
channels.description: Saga and state-machine execution, step by step.

channels.name: jobs
channels.description: Background workers: what was queued, and what could not be delivered.

channels.name: dictionary
channels.description: The Application Dictionary at run time: cache invalidation, and a column it describes that the database does not have.

channels.name: request
channels.description: One line per HTTP request the generated application answered, and the errors that reached the top of a handler.

channels.name: assistant
channels.description: The generated application's natural-language query add-on.
